newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S RAIFFEISEN ORGANISES 1.61 BLN BOND ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S RAIFFEISEN ORGANISES 1.61 BLN BOND ISSUE.

text.p: Hungary's Raiffeisen financial group is organising bond issues,to raise 1.11 billion forints for broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Rt and 600 million forints for the local government of Pecs city.
"Antenna Hungaria had financing needs in connection with investments required by the media law," Ivan Gara, Deputy General Director of Raiffeisen Unicbank told a news conference on Tuesday.
Zoltan Radnoty, director of Raiffeisen group member Raiffeisen Securities, said several series of bonds will be issued until the year 2002, totaling 1.11 billion forints.

The maturity of Antenna bonds will run from three months to five years and will have a floating rate. The interest rate of the first tranche, which is expected to be issued in late May or early June, will be linked to the benchmark DWIX index.
On April 24 the DWIX index was 20.78 percent.
The city of Pecs will also issue several series of bonds with maturities between three months and five years, either with floating or with fixed rate bonds and the bonds can also be discounted bonds.
Radnoty said Pecs will spend the money on general financing and some special projects.
The first series is expected to be issued by the end of May and the program is running until the end of 2004.
In both cases the bonds will be issued privately, to institutional investors.
Domestic bond issues have been relatively rare recently but mobile phone company Pannon GSM was issuing bonds totaling a nominal 25 billion forints.
